 THIS MFA IS FILED U/S. 173(1) OF MV ACT PRAYING TO ALLOW THIS APPEAL AND SET ASIDE THE IMPUGNED JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 26.11.2014 PASSED IN MVC NO.465/2012 ON THE FILE OF THE PRINCIPAL MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL AND PRINCIPAL DISTRICT JUDGE AT BIDAR, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION AND AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.3,60,900/-
IN SO FAR AS THE LIABILITY IS SADDLED UPON THE APPELLANT INSURANCE COMPANY AND TO REDUCE THE SAME IN CASE LIABILITY IS SADDLED UPON THE APPELLANT INSURANCE COMPANY.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Heard on admission.
2. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted his argument that the tribunal has not properly appreciated the evidence on record in a proper and perspective manner.
3. The admission of PW1 clearly reveals that deceased was not working as a driver of original respondent No.1 and therefore was only a borrower of said vehicle.
Hence, claim of the petition is liable to be rejected as against the appellant on the ground of maintainability.
Though, it may be sustainable only against the original against respondent No.3.
Therefore, the claimants have filed the claim petition under Section 163A of MV Act, claiming compensation in respect of death of Veerendra in the Motor vehicle accident.

4. In para 27 and 28 of the judgment, the tribunal has observed as under:
"On behalf of 2nd respondent, the Legal Officer of 2nd respondent is examined as R.W.1 and got marked documentary evidence as per Ex.R.1 to 3.
Ex.R.1 is the insurance policy, Ex.R.2 is the charge sheet and Ex.P.3 is the authorisation letter.
Upon perusing Ex.R.1 insurance policy which is package policy.
The package policy also covers the risk of the driver and whoever may be inmates in the Car.
During course of cross- examination R.W.1 admitted that under the package policy risk of the driver of the Car and also inmates of the Car are covered.

Further R.W.1 admitted in the evidence that, towards covering risk of the driver of the Car premium was The Manager Of vs Smt.Tanuja W/O Kiran Chanda And Ors on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5741438/
2 collected.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, R.W.1 in the cross-examination admits that as on the date and time of accident, the deceased was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the Car.

Therefore, upon considering the evidences on record, since insurance policy is package policy and also 2nd respondent had collected premium to cover the risk of the driver, therefore, eventhough deceased was driving the Car and met with accident, but 2nd respondent is liable to pay compensation according to the terms and condition of the policy, since risk towards driver of the Car is also covered.
Therefore, in this regard there is no merit in the argument canvassed by learned counsel for the 2nd respondent.

28. The counsel for the 2 respondent relied on the Judgement of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No. 7408 of 2007 in the case Christine Angela Kripalani Vs.
Florence Kripalani decided on 21-9-2012 and also by relying on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, 2008 (3) T.A.C. 204 (Karnataka) in the case Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Mahabunni and another. Therefore, submitted that the 2nd respondent is not liable to pay compensation.

entities.text:
Christine Angela Kripalani Vs.
Florence Kripalani
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Mahabunni and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above cited two judgments, the facts and circumstances are different from the instant case.

In the present case the insurance policy is package policy, but in the above stated judgments the fact that whether insurance policy is package policy or liability only is not forthcoming in the above cited judgments in the facts.
Therefore, when these factual matrix are considered the facts and circumstances in the above cited two cases and facts and circumstances in the present case are different.

In the present case, R.W.1 admitted that the insurance policy is package policy and risk of the driver of the Car and also inmates of the Car are covered and also towards covering the risk of the driver of the Car premium was collected and deceased was holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date and time of the accident.

Therefore, it is proved that,
the insurance policy is package policy and risk of the driver is also covered and premium was collected towards covering the risk of the driver.
Therefore, by virtue of the contract of insurance, 2nd respondent is liable to pay compensation.

Therefore,
with great respect to the above cited two judgments relied on the by the learned counsel for the 2nd respondent are not helpful to the 2nd respondent.
The court is of the opinion that 2nd respondent shall pay compensation to the petitioners by indemnifying 1st respondent and to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is held that the liability is joint and several.
Further, in view of the contract of insurance as per Ex.R.1 insurance policy, the 2nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent and pay compensation.

Accordingly, I answer above issue no.2 in the negative."
5.
A perusal of the judgment, I do not find any illegality, informality in the impugned judgment and award.
Hence, that there are no grounds to interfere in the impugned judgment and award passed by the MACT.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
